title: Why Hospitality in India is Buzzing (And What We’re Hearing on the Ground)
author: Jonathan Bush
excerpt: India’s hospitality scene is shifting fast, and we’re here for it. From guest expectations to digital check-ins, here’s what we’re learning directly from the leaders making it happen
body:
India’s hospitality scene is buzzing.

If you’ve been to Mumbai or Bengaluru recently, you’ll know what we mean. Hotels are packed, guests expect everything instantly, and the entire industry is in the middle of a digital shift that feels inevitable—and exciting.

In recent conversations with @Shiva from IHCL, we’re seeing the growing need for balancing scale with guest intimacy in India’s luxury hospitality sector. The demand for instant, seamless service is here, and hotels are looking to technology not as a replacement for warmth, but as a tool to keep up with guests who expect speed without losing the personal touch. It’s clear this innovation is new, and we’re excited that DialZero is leading this shift to help hotels make that balance possible.

We’re grateful to be in operations with forward-thinking leaders like Shiva and the teams at IHCL who are pushing the industry forward while staying true to what makes hospitality meaningful.

It’s not just about digital. It’s about speed.

A recent McKinsey report found that 75% of consumers expect assistance within five minutes of making contact online—and it’s not hard to see how this expectation carries into their hotel stay, where waiting for a towel or WiFi instructions feels like an eternity. Hotels in India are recognizing this, and the pressure to deliver “right now” service while maintaining quality is real.

For us at DialZero, it’s energizing to see hospitality in India embracing these changes. This shift isn’t about replacing warm service with cold automation. It’s about using the right tools to give guests what they want faster while freeing staff to focus on human connection—the very thing that makes hospitality feel like home.

We’re grateful to be part of this journey, learning alongside leaders who are pushing the industry forward while keeping its heart intact.

And if your hotel team is feeling the pressure to “move as fast as your guests,” we’d love to chat (over chai, obviously) about how you can keep pace while keeping your team’s sanity intact.

Because if there’s one thing we’ve learned in India, it’s that when hospitality booms, it really booms. And it’s better to be ready.
